corrections.proposed: built circa the 1930s (early 1930s per 2023 visit report)
corrections.why: The NHLR Built field reads circa 1930s, not a single year. 1930 comes from a directory listing, so the record should show the date as approximate.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 3,660 ft (1,116 m); firelookout.com and the Oregon directory give 3,664 ft. The record's 1115.6 m matches the NHLR figure. The gap is about 1 m.
NHLR says circa 1930s, the directory lists 1930, and a 2023 visit report says early 1930s. Story uses approximate early-1930s wording with the directory's 1930 as the single cited year.

notes_for_editor: Not a tower: the record's point kind is right, and the NHLR page describes an Osborne fire-finder in an enclosure. Build date is approximate (circa 1930s). The 1935 panorama note does not say who Osborne was, so the story does not link him to the finder's name. No fires, named staff or closure history were found in the sources read. Access: the finder is locked and used only in emergencies, and the pull-out is on a public road, so access is rated restricted. Photos on the NHLR and firelookout.com pages are credited to Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were captured, so none are added. One search returned a Forest Fire Lookout Association history page of the Osborne finder (firelookout.org/resources/plans/hist-osborne/) that was not read; it could add build and staffing detail. Cheryl Hill's table header was read on 2026-10-08: Unmanned is the STATUS column, and the last column is Accessible to Public (legal access only, per the directory's own note).
